title: style_findings@v1
description: A style critic's findings over one Russian technical article. Findings are PROPOSALS: each carries `decision`, which the human sets at the checkpoint before an editor applies anything. Layer 1 is mechanical and countable (dashes, quotes, address, calques, term drift); layer 2 is the machine-pattern hunt (impersonal passive, punctuation overload, three actors in one sentence, chained «не X, а Y», uniform sentence rhythm).

summary.description: Three to five sentences: the state of the text and its main ailments. Not a list of findings — the diagnosis behind them.

counters.description: Exact counts for the mechanical layer, one key per rule (`dash`, `quotes`, `address_ty`, calque tokens). Counted with the search tool, not estimated: a rule whose count is a guess cannot be a gate later.

dash.description: Hyphens standing in for an em dash in prose.

quotes.description: Straight quotes around Russian prose instead of « ».

address_ty.description: «ты»-forms in a text written as «вы» (whitelist zones excluded).

findings.description: One entry per defect. Empty is a valid, meaningful answer: a clean text by a criterion is reported as clean, never padded with invented findings.

id.description: Stable id within this report, e.g. F-1. The human refers to it when accepting or declining.

layer.description: 1 = mechanical (countable, safe to apply verbatim); 2 = stylistic (a judgement about the author's voice).

rule.description: Which criterion fired: dash, quotes, ellipsis, address, calque, term_drift, passive_inanimate, punctuation_overload, three_actors, not_x_but_y, rhythm.

line.description: 1-based line in the article, so the editor edits the right occurrence rather than the first textual match.

quote.description: The offending text verbatim — the evidence. Stated BEFORE the reasoning, never reconstructed from memory.

reason.description: Why this violates the named criterion. Reasoning comes before the verdict, not after it.

before.description: Exact text to replace. Must occur in the article verbatim, or the editor cannot apply it safely.

after.description: The replacement. Preserves meaning, the article's terminology, and roughly the original length — a fix that inflates the sentence is a rewrite, not a fix.

severity.description: error: mechanically wrong (typography, calque with an exact Russian verb). warn: reads as machine-written. info: preference.

decision.description: Set by the critic to `pending` and by the HUMAN at the checkpoint. The editor applies `accept` only; `pending` counts as not accepted.

note.description: Optional: why the human decided this way, or the critic's own uncertainty (e.g. a suspected deliberate stylisation zone worth asking about).

terms.description: Terminology audit: one entry per special term of the article. Catches two defects a sentence-level pass cannot see — synonyms for one concept mixed without explanation, and a term used before it is introduced.

variants.description: Every form the article uses for this one concept.

defined_line.description: Where the term is introduced. Greater than first_use_line means the reader met it before it was explained.

deliberate_zones.description: Passages that break a rule on purpose (an ironic aside addressing the reader as «ты» in a text written as «вы»). Reported, not counted as defects — and worth asking the author about rather than silently fixing.
